title: More half-waves in a box
hook: Change quantum number and predict allowed wavelength.
misconception: allowed wavelength doubles when quantum number doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply λ_n = 2L/n to compare allowed wavelength when quantum number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a one-dimensional infinite square well of fixed width with allowed positive integer quantum numbers, λ_n = 2L/n. When quantum number doubles, allowed wavelength becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model λ_n = 2L/n; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a one-dimensional infinite square well of fixed width with allowed positive integer quantum numbers, with a nonzero initial result. If quantum number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on allowed wavelength?
recall.why: Apply λ_n = 2L/n under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
